articleBlocks: At first, Crows and Ebony pointed in a few different directions, so the board still felt wider than one exact category.
One tempting read was "dark birds only". Crows strongly point that way, but Ebony, Ripe olives, Charcoal, and Asphalt push the board beyond birds.
Another nearby read was "black materials". Ebony, Charcoal, and Asphalt can pull the board toward materials, but Crows and Ripe olives make the answer broader: things that are black.
Once I read the set as things that are black, examples like crows and ebony stopped feeling loose and started landing cleanly.
Ripe olives, Charcoal, and Asphalt keep confirming black as the shared trait, which is what makes the board feel like one exact set.

The answer was "Things that are black". More precisely, every clue names a thing that can be black, which is why this reading fits better than "dark birds only" or "black materials" once the full set is checked.
solutionNarrative: I first read Crows and Ebony too literally and drifted toward dark birds or dark materials. Crows could suggest birds, and Ebony could suggest a material or color, so the board still felt open instead of solved.
Ripe olives changed the direction because ripe olives are commonly black, giving the board a testable shared trait instead of a loose topic.
I then checked crows, ebony, charcoal, and asphalt. Those checks mattered because each one is a normal black thing, so I was not forcing five separate hints into one bag.

That left very little room for the earlier false start. The answer was "Things that are black", and the last step was simply making sure every clue used that same reading cleanly before treating the solve as finished.
